title: Lekalo Storage Engine Profile
description: Closed independent attachment contract declaring one project's storage engine profile (issue #69): the exact engine identity and version pin, the declared SQL-shaping policies (JSON, enum, array, time, pagination, identifier quoting), tenancy enforcement, optimistic-versioning policy, checked-mode introspection declaration, test-database lifecycle, extension allow-list, and the digest binding to the storage-projection attachment it profiles. The profile is pure declaration and validation data: it never executes, never connects, never carries credentials, hosts, URLs, runtime values, or provider output; every database reference is one opaque connection name token resolved outside this family.

attachmentRevision.description: The exact revision of this attachment; a change is a wire-layer fact.

modelRef.description: The exact bound source Model contract: accepted version plus canonical digest.

irRef.description: The exact bound IR contract: accepted identity plus canonical digest.

projectionRef.description: The canonical digest of the exact storage-projection attachment this profile consumes. A profile can never float free of a declared projection.

engine.description: The closed engine vocabulary of v1.

engineVersion.description: The exact canonical version of the target server; it must resolve to one supported row of the owner-published version matrix or the profile is refused as unsupported.

tenancy.description: The explicit tenant isolation enforcement of this profile; never implied by a tenant key column alone.

concurrency.description: The declared optimistic-versioning policy of this profile.

introspection.description: The checked-mode schema introspection declaration. Absent means no introspection capability is claimed.

testLifecycle.description: The isolated test-database lifecycle. Absent means no test-database capability is claimed.

extensions.description: The closed extension allow-list. An observed extension outside this list is reported as unsupported, never silently coerced.

connectionName.description: One opaque connection name token. It is resolved against a connection registry outside this contract; credentials, hosts, URLs, and parameters are unrepresentable by grammar.

sessionVariable.description: One bounded custom GUC name for the tenant session variable.

identifierQuote.description: The emitted-identifier quoting policy; v1 has exactly one deterministic answer.

json.description: The JSON column policy: jsonb by default, the json type only by explicit opt-in.

enum.description: The enum policy: a bounded CHECK predicate, or a native engine enum type created per column.

array.description: The array policy: native engine arrays, JSON encoding, or an explicit refusal for declared array fields.

instant.description: The instant column type; the timezoned type is the only default.

local.description: Whether the timezone-naive local timestamp type may be rendered at all; forbidden is the honest default.

offset.description: Whether LIMIT/OFFSET pagination may be rendered.

cursor.description: The cursor rendering: keyset row comparison over the declared sort and identity tie-breaker.

enforcement.description: The tenant isolation mechanism: none, an application-level scope, or engine row-level security (which requires a tenant key on every covered table).

force.description: True when row-level security applies to the table owner too (FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY).

versioning.description: The optimistic-versioning mechanism: a declared technical version column compared and incremented on every update, or none.

waitPolicy.description: Whether lock acquisition waits or fails fast.

mode.description: The only accepted introspection mode: checked. Unchecked schema observation is unrepresentable by construction.

scopes.description: The bounded schema allow-list the adapter may observe.

isolation.description: The test isolation boundary: one database per run, one schema per run, or one transaction rolled back per case.

provision.description: How the test surface is created: created then dropped, cloned from a template, or assumed to exist.

cleanup.description: How the test surface is cleaned: dropped, truncated, or rolled back.

production.description: The only wire value: production access through the test lifecycle is forbidden.

state.description: Whether the extension may be created on demand or must already exist.
